subject: Procurement: PO vs Card decisioning & vendor onboarding - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Wang <sarah.wang@finopsco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement & PO vs Card - Redwood Inference next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks again for a great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so your AP/procurement team has what they need: 

Summary from call:
- Primary use: inference for customer-facing features (chat + embeddings) with ~5M tokens/month expected year 1.
- Procurement constraints: AP prefers PO for vendor spend > $50k/year; corporate card allowed for misc/one-off purchases.
- Vendor onboarding: they need W-9, COI (if requested), vendor form and standard security questionnaire (we can provide SOC 2 + penetration test summary).

Options we discussed:
1) Standard PO (preferred by your AP) — Redwood will accept PO and provide an invoice net-30 / net-45 as agreed.
2) AWS Marketplace — if you prefer to charge to your AWS account, we can offer procurement via Marketplace with your normal AWS billing cadence.
3) Card — feasible for initial POC spend under your AP thresholds.

Attached: high-level estimate + SOW stub (Redwood_STD_SOW_estimate.pdf) and vendor onboarding template. I also added a short mutual action plan below to keep momentum.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
- FinOpsCo: confirm preferred procurement path (PO vs Marketplace) and estimated annual committed spend — due: Wed Oct 1
- Redwood: provide vendor onboarding docs (W-9, COI if requested), draft contract terms and final quote — due: Fri Oct 2
- Both: schedule procurement intro call with AP (if needed) — propose Tue Oct 6

If AP needs a dedicated vendor onboarding packet, say the word and I’ll loop in our vendor onboarding specialist.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Aditya to get you the security artifacts.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0129

Attachment: Redwood_STD_SOW_estimate.pdf
Attachment: vendor_onboarding_template.docx

From: Sarah Wang <sarah.wang@finopsco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: AP Team <ap@finopsco.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement & PO vs Card - Redwood Inference next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the estimate. A few clarifications from AP and procurement: 

- AP policy: we require a PO for new vendors if annual spend > $50k. That means for production rollouts we will need a PO and vendor onboarding completed before the first invoice.
- Vendor onboarding: AP wants a completed vendor form (I attached the intake form in this reply), W-9, and proof of insurance (COI) only if annual spend > $100k.
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is preferred by some business units because it goes through their cloud budget, but central procurement prefers a direct PO for enterprise agreements.

Two asks for your team: 
1) Can Redwood accept a PO and invoice net-30?
2) Can you provide the W-9 and a SOC 2 summary (or the SOC 2 report via an NDA/portal)?

If both are OK we’ll start our vendor onboarding and aim to issue a PO in the first two weeks of Oct.

Thanks,
Sarah
Head of Procurement | FinOpsCo
sarah.wang@finopsco.com

Attachment: FinOps_Vendor_Intake_Form.pdf

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement & PO vs Card - Redwood Inference next steps

Hi Sarah — yes to both. Confirming details: 

- Redwood accepts PO and can invoice net-30 (we can also support net-45 for new enterprise agreements on request).
- I’ve attached our W-9 and a redacted SOC 2 summary; for the full report we can provide access via our security portal or execute an NDA if your compliance team prefers.

Next steps from our side: 
- I’m attaching the draft SOW/estimate (Redwood_STD_SOW_estimate.pdf) and the vendor onboarding template.
- If you’re planning a standalone PO, please confirm the billing contact and the legal name to put on the invoice (FinOpsCo, Inc. or FinOpsCo LLC?).
- If you’d like AWS Marketplace, we can provide a Marketplace offer but note Marketplace billing will follow AWS billing cycles and potentially different discount structure.

DocuSign link for standard T&Cs (for reference): https://www.docusign.com/prepare/ABC123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FINOPS-2026-0483

I’ll loop Aditya to see if we should propose a short AP intro call to speed vendor onboarding.

Best,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Procurement & PO vs Card - Redwood Inference next steps (internal)

Marissa — quick guidance for the thread and ops: 

- PO + net-30 is standard and fine. Finance will set up FinOpsCo as a vendor once they receive the vendor intake form + W-9. We should expect 7-10 business days for vendor setup in most cases.
- For SOC 2 report sharing: use our secure portal link and offer an NDA if the customer insists. Don’t email the full report.
- Marketplace: If FinOpsCo wants Marketplace we can mirror equivalent pricing but we’ll need their billing account and to coordinate with partner ops. Marketplace often slows down procurement for enterprise because business units request separate PO approvals.

Suggested next steps to keep deal moving: 
1) Ask Sarah to confirm legal entity name + billing contact (we need exact PO fields).
2) Provide the vendor intake form pre-filled where possible to shorten AP back-and-forth (Marissa — you can attach a filled copy).
3) Offer a short 30-min vendor onboarding call with AP on Oct 6 if they want it.

I’ll stand by to help with pricing nuances if they push on committed discount tiers.

— Aditya
Head of Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
